name: Söll
kurzbeschreibung: Heart of the ski world: Wilder Kaiser–Brixental, with traditional Tiroler hospitality and 90 kilometers of ski runs.
beschreibung:
Overview

Söll is located at an altitude of 703 meters in the scenic valley basin of Sölllandl in the Kufstein district of the Tyrolean Unterland. Framed by the limestone crags of the Wilder Kaiser range to the north and the panoramic summit of Mount Hohe Salve (1,829 m) to the south, Söll forms part of the celebrated Wilder Kaiser holiday region alongside Scheffau, Ellmau, and Going. Home to approximately 3,750 residents, Söll is a lively, welcoming alpine village blending deep-rooted traditions with premier sports facilities. In winter, it serves as a central hub of the vast SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental ski area and reigns as Austria’s premier night-skiing capital. During the summer months, Söll captivates visitors with the award-winning Hexenwasser mountain adventure park and is famous as a filming backdrop for the popular television drama Der Bergdoktor.

History

Archaeological evidence points to Bavarian settlement in the valley basin around 600 AD. Söll was first documented in 1217 as sel, deriving from the Middle High German selida, meaning a lodge or settlement. Following the War of the Succession of Landshut in 1504, Emperor Maximilian I permanently incorporated the territory into the County of Tyrol. The architectural pride of the village is the late Baroque parish church of Saints Peter and Paul, affectionately referred to as the Söllandler Bauerndom (Peasants' Cathedral) due to its monumental proportions. Built between 1764 and 1768 and consecrated in 1771, it ranks among Tyrol's finest Rococo ecclesiastical buildings, featuring luminous ceiling frescoes by Christoph Anton Mayr. High above on the peak of Hohe Salve stands the pilgrimage chapel of Saint John the Baptist, first recorded in 1589 as Austria’s highest pilgrimage church.

Getting there

Söll boasts effortless road and rail access. Motorists approaching from Germany or Salzburg exit the A12 Inntal motorway at Kufstein-Süd, following state road B173 (Eibergstraße) for just ten minutes directly into Söll (toll-free driving is possible via Bavarian state roads). Approaching from Innsbruck, take exit Wörgl-Ost and follow the B178 federal road for 12 kilometers. Rail travelers arrive at Wörgl Central Station, a major Austrian transport hub for Railjet and ICE trains, or at Kufstein station. VVT regional bus line 4060 runs frequently from Wörgl station to Söll village and the cable car terminal. In summer, the complimentary KaiserJet shuttle bus operates daily between Söll, Scheffau, Ellmau, and Going.

Tips

During summer, visit the award-winning Hexenwasser adventure park at the Hochsöll mid-station, featuring over 60 sensory stations based on local witch legends, Austria's longest barefoot trail (over 4 km), a walk-in beehive, and interactive water laboratories. Continue by gondola to the summit of Hohe Salve (1,829 m) to admire 360-degree vistas taking in over 70 peaks above 3,000 meters, along with the mountaintop chapel and giant sundial. In winter, explore the 270 kilometers of pistes in the SkiWelt, or enjoy Austria’s largest night-skiing arena with ten kilometers of floodlit runs and two illuminated toboggan tracks. TV fans can walk to the Köglhof farmstead on Mount Bromberg, featured as the Gruberhof in Der Bergdoktor, or take a swim in Lake Ahornsee.
